2.2.6.4-r1.burton_quote: Nepenthes of Homer, Helena’s bowl, Venus’ girdle, so renowned of old to expel grief and care, to cause mirth and gladness of heart

2.2.6.4-r10.burton_quote: The whole nation beyond all other mortal men, is most given to banqueting and feasts; for they prolong them many hours together, with dainty cheer, exquisite music, and facete jesters, and afterwards they fall a-dancing and courting their mistresses

2.2.6.4-r11.burton_quote: Live merrily O my friends, free from cares, perplexity, anguish, grief of mind, live merrily

2.2.6.4-r12.burton_quote: again and again I request you to be merry, if anything trouble your hearts, or vex your souls, neglect and contemn it

2.2.6.4-r13.burton_quote: Contemn the world (saith he) and count all that is in it vanity and toys, this only covet all thy life long; be not curious, or oversolicitous in anything, but with a well-composed and contented estate to enjoy thyself, and above all things to be merry

2.2.6.4-r2.burton_quote: Let them use hunting, sports, plays, jests, merry company, as Rhasis prescribes, which will not let the mind be molested, a cup of good drink now and then, hear music, and have such companions with whom they are especially delighted
2.2.6.4-r2.translation: and a change of place, and joy

2.2.6.4-r3.burton_quote: an especial remedy against melancholy, to hear and see singing, dancing, masquers, mummers, to converse with such merry fellows, and fair maids

2.2.6.4-r5.burton_quote: that were frequently seen in Epicurus’ garden

2.2.6.4-r6.translation: As a girl reclining sweetly on the bed, etc.

2.2.6.4-r7.burton_quote: ride a cock-horse with his Children

citations.display: Valerius Maximus, *Memorable Deeds and Sayings*, book 8

2.2.6.4-r7.translation: and was laughed at by Alcibiades.

2.2.6.4-r8.burton_quote: now and then play the most egregious fool in his carriage, and was so much given to jesters, players, and childish sports, to make himself merry, that he that should but consider his gravity on the one part, his folly and lightness on the other, would surely say, there were two distinct persons in him

2.2.6.4-r9.burton_quote: because laughter and merriment was to season their labours and modester life
